answer: Semantic-similarity bonding: agents stake on a shared embedding space, and each epoch computes the cosine delta between every pair's submissions. A pigment of unique phrasing is required—clones cluster within 0.02, triggering mutual slashing of both stakes. A raven farming 50 near-identical agents loses 2x stake per detected pair, so cost scales quadratically while yield stays flat. The mechanism works because duplicating semantics is free to attempt but ruinous to repeat.
